## Technical Blog Articles — Full Summaries (5 Articles)

### post_1 — The Complete Steam Turbine Overhauling Checklist for Plant Engineers
- **Slug**: steam-turbine-overhauling-checklist | **Date**: 2026-03-15 | **Read time**: 8 min

7 phases: (1) Pre-shutdown planning 4–6 weeks before — scope, spares procurement, tool mobilisation, lube oil flush rig, ex-OEM engineer arrangement, condition monitoring baseline. (2) Shutdown & isolation — LOTO all energy sources (steam, lube oil, condensate, control air), full drain. (3) Disassembly & inspection — record all clearances pre-removal; measure rotor run-out at journal, thrust collar, coupling face; photograph every stage. (4) Workshop repairs — journal grinding and dynamic balancing (ISO 1940/API 670), carbon ring replacement, labyrinth packing, babbitt re-pour if required. (5) Reassembly & alignment — new gaskets, OEM torques, laser alignment (turbine-gearbox-generator), record all post-assembly clearances. (6) Lube oil flushing — target ISO 4406:99 Class 16/14/11; retain pre/post sampling reports. (7) Commissioning — OEM pre-commissioning procedure; monitor vibration, bearing temperatures, lube oil pressure; confirm ESV and governor operation.

---

### post_2 — How Lube Oil Contamination Destroys Turbine Bearings
- **Slug**: lube-oil-contamination-turbine-bearings | **Date**: 2026-02-28 | **Read time**: 6 min

3 contamination types: (1) Solid particles — 1–10 µm particles cause three-body abrasion in oil film; solution: ISO 16889 beta-ratio ≥200 filter elements + breather filter; target 16/14/11. (2) Water ingress — 200 ppm free water reduces film strength; sources: condenser leaks, steam gland failure, cooler tube failure; solution: WaterSorp offline elements + monthly Karl Fischer sampling. (3) Oil oxidation — varnish from thermal degradation; detected by acid number (AN) trending; prevention: correct oil change intervals, WaterSorp filtration, cool tank temperature. Action schedule: check filter ΔP weekly (replace at 3.5–4 bar), inspect breather monthly, oil sampling every 30 days, flush after every major repair.

---

### post_3 — Reverse Engineering Turbine Spares: How We Recreate Obsolete Components in India
- **Slug**: reverse-engineering-turbine-spares-india | **Date**: 2026-01-20 | **Read time**: 7 min

5-step process: (1) Component acquisition — worn/broken part received; visual assessment; measurable surfaces identified. (2) 3D laser scanning & CMM — point cloud for complex profiles (blades, nozzles, diaphragms); CMM for rotational parts; all critical dimensions, concentricity, threads, keyways recorded to ±0.02 mm. (3) PMI testing — XRF or OES identifies exact alloy composition (critical: 12% Cr vs 1% Cr-Mo). (4) Engineering drawing generation — full GD&T: dimensions, tolerances, surface finish, pre/post heat treatment, material spec, inspection requirements. (5) Machining & QC — rough machining → heat treatment (stress relieving, Q&T, nitriding if required) → final precision machining; dynamic balancing to ISO 1940/API 670; inspection at each stage. Lead time: 4–8 weeks. OEM import: 12–18 months.

---

### post_4 — Belliss & Morcom Turbine Common Faults — Field Guide for Indian Plants
- **Slug**: belliss-morcom-turbine-common-faults-india | **Date**: 2026-03-18 | **Read time**: 8 min

4 common faults: (1) High vibration — root causes: rotor imbalance (deposit buildup), journal bearing wear, turbine-gearbox misalignment from pipe strain/foundation settling. Diagnosis: 1× dominant = imbalance/misalignment; 2× dominant = looseness; sub-sync = oil whirl. (2) Governor hunting — centrifugal fly-ball wear, incorrect droop, boiler supply pressure fluctuation (>±0.5 bar makes governor authority insufficient). Check boiler stability before dismantling governor. (3) Steam gland leakage — worn labyrinth strips, incorrect gland steam pressure, shaft eccentricity. Check shaft runout (>0.05 mm → assess rotor); check gland steam is dry. (4) Lube oil high temperature/low pressure — high temp: cooler fouled (clean tube bundle); low pressure: relief valve incorrect, filter ΔP high (replace element), oil pump worn.

---

### post_5 — How to Read an ISO 4406 Lube Oil Cleanliness Report
- **Slug**: iso-4406-lube-oil-cleanliness-guide | **Date**: 2026-04-05 | **Read time**: 6 min

Key facts: ISO 4406:99 code = three numbers (e.g. 18/16/13) for particle counts at ≥4 µm(c) / ≥6 µm(c) / ≥14 µm(c). Each code number = a particle count range (code 16 = 320–640 particles/mL; code 18 = 1,280–2,560/mL). Each step up = doubling of contamination. API 614 target for turbine bearing lube: 16/14/11. Triveni/Siemens EHC governing: 15/13/10. Alert level: 6 µm code at 17 or above → investigate immediately. Damage model: 100× more damaging particles at 20/18/15 vs 16/14/11. "(c)" suffix confirms ISO 11171 optical counter calibration — do not compare with older uncalibrated reports. Action: if 6 µm code ≥ 17, check filter ΔP, inspect breather, sample upstream/downstream to locate contamination entry; if water >0.1%, install WaterSorp elements and schedule offline flushing.
